description:
CSK in IPL 2024 was a story of fine margins and a late twist that kept fans on edge.

Chennai Super Kings finished 5th in the league stage with 14 points from 14 matches (7 wins, 7 losses). They missed the playoffs on net run rate after losing the final league game to RCB, who edged ahead on the table. It was only the third time the franchise did not make the playoffs.

Ruturaj Gaikwad led in his first season as captain and set the tone with the bat. He scored 583 runs in 14 innings at an average of 53.00 and a strike rate of 141.16, including a highest score of 108*. His form kept CSK in the hunt through a streaky second half.

The bowling group produced telling spells. Tushar Deshpande finished as the leading wicket-taker for CSK with 17 wickets in 13 innings (best 4/27). Mustafizur Rahman added 14 in 9 matches (best 4/29), offering control at the death. Matheesha Pathirana took 13 in just 6 games (best 4/28) and returned the side’s best bowling average of 13.00. These bursts created chances that the team could not always convert into wins.

Key takeaways for anyone tracking CSK in IPL 2024: • League stage: 5th place, level on points with 4th, behind on NRR
• Record: 7 wins, 7 losses (14 points)
• Captain: Ruturaj Gaikwad (583 runs, 108*, 53.00 average, 141.16 SR)
• Wickets: Tushar Deshpande 17; Mustafizur Rahman 14; Matheesha Pathirana 13

CSK in IPL 2024 started strong, but inconsistency in the latter half proved costly. The squad stayed competitive until the final night, showing depth with bat and ball yet falling short by the slimmest measure. If you want quick facts, player numbers, and match context in one place, keep CSK in IPL 2024 bookmarked and revisit the season that turned on net run rate.
name: IPL 2024

description:
CSK in IPL 2025 was a season that never found rhythm. Chennai Super Kings played 14 matches, won 4, lost 10, and finished 10th on the table. It was their lowest finish and the second straight year without playoffs. They were the first side knocked out of the race, a stark turn for a team used to big May nights.

The quick facts for CSK in IPL 2025 tell the story. They played 14 matches, with 4 wins and 10 losses, finishing last. At home in Chepauk, they struggled, losing 5 of 7 matches. Their playoff run never took shape, and elimination came early in the league stage.

Several factors contributed to this downturn. Batting failed to fire in the powerplays, and finishes lacked impact. Injuries in the early stages forced constant changes in the XI. Strategies felt stagnant, with combinations rotating but results staying the same. Even a mid-season leadership change, when MS Dhoni took over for a stretch, could not reverse the slide.

There were still standout performances in a lean year. Shivam Dube led the run charts for CSK with 357 runs, while Ravindra Jadeja contributed 301 and anchored the middle order. Noor Ahmad had a breakthrough season with 24 wickets, finishing as the second-highest wicket-taker in the league. Khaleel Ahmed added 15 wickets to the tally. The bowling unit produced moments of control, but without big totals on the board, they often had little to defend.

CSK in IPL 2025 underlined how fine margins define T20 cricket. A slow start can leave even a strong side chasing the table. Home advantage only matters if it translates to wins, and batting clarity will be crucial in future campaigns. For fans tracking the season for form, fantasy picks, or off-season rebuild plans, the campaign was tough, but the foundation for a reset is in place.
name: IPL 2025
